basis: Defined by intellectual disability, epilepsy and motor abnormalities; ear and facial dysmorphism do not establish functional injury; hearing loss is only occasional.
Leukocyte dysfunction causes immunodeficiency; platelet dysfunction causes severe bleeding. Hepatomegaly alone does not establish liver injury; osteopetrosis occurs in <30%.
Congenital muscular dystrophy and cerebellar atrophy are both defining lesions.
Parasitic infection produces extensive cutaneous lesions; definition explicitly excludes visceral involvement.
Cerebral white-matter disease with subcortical cysts, seizures, ataxia and progressive motor dysfunction.
Adenocarcinoma originates in gastric mucosa; hereditary cancer risks elsewhere do not establish involvement.
Disease of peripheral arteries; claudication alone does not establish muscle injury, and visceral organ infarction is not common across the umbrella.
Umbrella of inborn metabolic absorption and transport defects; no additional organ is consistently damaged across the group.
Organic aciduria; developmental disability, seizures and spasticity occur in 80-99%. Liver dysfunction, cardiomyopathy, cataracts and hearing loss each occur in <30%.
Neutral lipid storage disease characterized by pathological triglyceride deposition in myocardium and coronary vessels.
Lymphoid-cell malignancy umbrella encompassing T/NK-cell leukemias and lymphomas; no consistent extranodal organ across subtypes.
Congenital structural defect of the radius with failure of bony union.
Broad lymphoid/immune-system umbrella encompassing nodal, splenic and lymphatic disorders; heterogeneous mechanisms make this axis assignment approximate.
Lacrimal obstruction, dystonia/intellectual disability and digital malformations define syndrome; hearing loss occurs in 30-79%. Cleft palate (30-79%) omitted by cap.
Interferonopathy defined by aortic calcification/stenosis and skeletal disease; dental dysplasia is defining. Chronic psoriasiform skin disease omitted by cap.
Localized cutaneous amyloid deposition causes persistent pruritic, lichenified skin lesions; systemic amyloidosis is not part of this concept.
Glycine metabolism defect described in one patient; fatigue and elevated CK suggest muscle involvement but do not firmly establish a damaging myopathy.
Nonsyndromic progressive sensorineural hearing loss, reported in 19/19 patients.
Defined by loss of liver function; no additional directly damaged organ is established across acute and chronic forms.
Hypertrophic adenoid tissue affects the nasopharyngeal airway; associated otitis media is a separately diagnosed disease.
Autoimmune cerebellar disease causes ataxia; absence of characteristic antibodies does not remove the immune mechanism.
Inherited retinal rod-cone degeneration with reduced vision; macular edema and peripapillary atrophy remain within the ocular axis.
Neurodevelopmental disorder of reduced brain/head growth; subtype-specific ocular or skeletal abnormalities do not apply across the umbrella.
Spinal/brainstem motor-neuron degeneration causes muscle denervation and atrophy in nearly all. Respiratory failure reflects muscle weakness rather than direct lung injury.
GnRH deficiency, olfactory dysfunction and cardiac malformations define syndrome. Renal agenesis occurs in 30-79%; hearing loss and cleft palate (30-79%) omitted by cap.
